=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangements observed)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at nodes)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit is composed of multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (leaflets are arranged along a central axis with one terminal leaflet present at the apex)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (each compound leaf has approximately 7 leaflets, with a terminal leaflet and 3 pairs on either side)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in pairs or whorls)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with a broad base tapering to a pointed apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaflets end in a sharp, pointed tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf base tapers to the petiolule, forming a wedge shape)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off at angles)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running parallel to each other and closely spaced)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface appears glossy, reflecting light, likely due to waxy cuticle)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, barely visible, connecting leaflets to rachis)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, without wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly thickened, typical of young woody seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green to dark green (stem is primarily green, darkening toward base)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudation visible upon inspection)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus visible at leaflet or leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: Some leaflets show minor damage, including holes and slight discoloration, likely from environmental exposure or minor physical abrasion. The seedling is marked with a pink tag and white label, indicating it is part of a monitoring or research plot. The surrounding forest floor is moist and covered with leaf litter and small ferns, consistent with a shaded understory environment, though habitat is not explicitly annotated per rules.
